sources.entry: zoneinfo - (Python standard library) IANA time zone support. Brings the tz database into Python.

summary.name: zoneinfo
summary.one_liner: Python standard library module (added in 3.9) that provides IANA time zone support for datetime objects, backed by the system tz database or the tzdata PyPI package.
use_cases: attach a named time zone to a Python datetime
handle daylight saving time transitions in datetime arithmetic
convert UTC timestamps to local time zones
list available IANA time zone names
ship cross-platform time zone data with tzdata dependency
summary.what_it_does: The module provides ZoneInfo, a concrete datetime.tzinfo implementation that represents an IANA time zone by key such as America/Los_Angeles. Datetimes attached to it handle DST transitions during arithmetic, and the fold attribute (PEP 495) disambiguates ambiguous local times. Time zone data is read from the system database, with a fallback to the first-party tzdata package on PyPI. The page also documents configuring the search path via compile-time TZPATH, the PYTHONTZPATH environment variable, and reset_tzpath(), plus pickling behavior and helper functions such as available_timezones().
notable: Standard library since Python 3.9, implements PEP 615
Caches ZoneInfo instances so the same key returns the same object
Falls back to the tzdata PyPI package when no system tz data exists
Supports the fold attribute from PEP 495 for ambiguous times
caveats: Windows systems lack an IANA database, so cross-platform projects should depend on tzdata
Objects built from a file via from_file() cannot be pickled
If neither system data nor tzdata is present, ZoneInfo calls raise ZoneInfoNotFoundError
